data.name: Anton
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Antonios was a name given to a goddess. This name has its origins in the ancient Greek language, and it was believed to mean 'priceless one'. In Christianity, Antonius is also the name of a saint who was a monk and a hermit. He is revered for his commitment to living a simple, pious life and is a patron saint of monks.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the value and worth of an individual in the eyes of God and the spiritual community.

in_hebrew.name: אנטון
in_hebrew.meaning: בעל חסד, יקר, אדם רב ערך
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אנטון נגזר מהשם היווני אנטון, שפירושו 'בעל חסד' או 'יקר'. הוא קשור למושגים של ערך וגדלות, ומשקף תכונות של אדם רב ערך ויקר.

in_greek.name: Αντών
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Αντών προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'Αντίος', που σημαίνει 'αντίος' ή 'πολύτιμος'. Στο πλαίσιο της παράδοσης Χριστιανική, το όνομα αντανακλά την έννοια του να είσαι πολύτιμος ή ανώτερος.

in_latin.name: Anton
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Anton derivatur ex Graeco 'Αντών', quod significat 'inestimabilis' vel 'pretiosus'. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc reflectit notionem magnitatis et valoris spiritualis.

in_english.name: Anton
in_english.long_meaning: The name Anton originates from the Greek 'Αντών' (Anton), meaning 'inestimable' or 'priceless'. It carries connotations of great value and high esteem. Historically, the name has been used in Christian tradition to signify someone of significant spiritual worth. The name Anton has been borne by several saints and martyrs, adding to its spiritual significance.

saint_reference.note: Several saints have borne variations of the name Anton, including Saint Anthony of Egypt, a prominent Christian saint and hermit.

data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Antonius is celebrated as a saint who embodied the essence of living a holy and humble life. His commitment to living a pious life, isolated from the distractions of the world, serves as an inspiration to Christians around the world. The spiritual significance of the name Anton is rooted in its connection to this saint, representing a dedication to a simple and godly life.

historical_references.reference: Saint Antoninus of Florence, born in 1389, was a Dominican friar and a renowned theologian, preacher, and biblical scholar. He was a close friend and advisor to Pope Leo X.

Saint Antoninus of Padua, born in 1195, was a Franciscan friar, preacher, and doctor of the Church. He was known for his great devotion to the Eucharist and the Virgin Mary, and is considered the patron saint of travelers.
